messages:
infra-bot: ALERT: High Xid/ECC error rate detected on gpu-node-47. Auto-evac threshold crossed. Investigate now.

maria: seeing repeated nv-host-channel errors + driver reset in dmesg, looks like Xid 13 bursts.

cheng: confirmed. Telemetry shows correctable ECC spikes across GPUs 0-3, memory parity warnings ~ every 20s.

sam: customer impact? any latency or failed requests surfaced in prod?

maria: yes — a subset of inference pods on node-47 are restarting intermittently, 504s for ~5% of requests from dedicated pool.

ops-bot: paging: @oncall infra (cheng) @pagerduty oncall (sam). Escalation policy: open incident.

cheng: starting triage — tailing kubelet logs and container logs. Attaching quick snippet:

```
Mar 15 03:12:09 gpu-node-47 kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 13, PID=20412 pbit=0
Mar 15 03:12:09 gpu-node-47 nvidia: GPU 0: ECC correctable error count incremented
Mar 15 03:12:29 gpu-node-47 kubelet: Pod "inference-xyz" container crashed with signal 7
```

rene: any recent driver or kernel rollouts in that rack?

maria: no driver updates in last 72h, but we did bump CUDA minor patch on node-45 earlier (different rack).

sam: mitigation plan: 1) cordon node-47, 2) drain with --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data, 3) soft-reboot GPU driver (nvidia-persistenced + modprobe), 4) if flapping persists, reprovision node. Agree?

alex: add step: snapshot kube events and KV cache metrics before drain so we can correlate evictions with KV cache OOMs.

cheng: running drain now: `kubectl drain gpu-node-47 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60` — will watch pod terminations.

ops-bot: NOTE: starting automated fallback: route new dedicated requests away from region-rack-3 for 10m.

maria: while draining, noticed one pod logs show `kvcache: allocation failed: out of memory` right before container crash. Could be KVCACHE OOM triggering driver resets.

rene: good catch — if KVCACHE is OOMing it can cascade into NV driver faults. Check per-container cache size and recent traffic spike.

cheng: performed `nvidia-smi --query` and driver reset shows 7 resets in the last 15m. Will attempt `sudo systemctl restart nvidia-persistenced` then `sudo rmmod nvidia_uvm && sudo modprobe nvidia_uvm` to clear kernel UVM state. Proceeding.

sam: keep customer comms: outreach to the two affected customers (IDs: C-824, C-391) — minimal request failures but steady degradations since 03:10 UTC. I can draft a short note.

alex: after driver restart, GPU stats show ECC error rate dropping but one GPU still has elevated correctables. Recommend leaving node cordoned for now and schedule hardware diag if correctables persist.

maria: post-driver-restart telemetry: Xid spikes stopped, kernel logs clean for 3 minutes but kvcache OOMs still present during heavy tails. I suspect workload pattern + slightly leaky cache config hit memory pressure.

cheng: I'll reconfigure inference pods on this node to use reduced KV cache (env VAR: KV_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES=25000 -> 15000) and redeploy canary on a healthy node to validate.

sam: handoff plan: if stable for next 15m, mark incident as mitigated and create follow-up ticket for hardware bench and memory-scan on GPU 2. If it flaps again, we escalate to hardware team and initiate reprovision.

ops-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigation in progress — node cordoned, driver restarted, requests routed away. Customer impact reduced to <1% errors.

maria: adding runbook notes: possible causes: ECC hardware degradation, KVCACHE OOM cascade, workload-induced memory pressure. Next steps: hardware diag, review kvcache defaults, add alert for KVCACHE OOM rate.

cheng: assigning follow-up: TICKET-INC-4872 -> hardware diag & replace GPU if ECC correctables persist; OWNER: hw-ops. Also TICKET-ENG-9201 -> autoscaling and kvcache config review; OWNER: eng-runtime.

sam: I notified customer contacts and logged an incident advisory. Will update if we see any regression.

maria: handing off to follow-up oncall @ 04:00 UTC (sam). Leaving node cordoned.

ops-bot: HANDOFF: oncall next shift acknowledged. Incident status: monitored.

cheng: closing realtime thread — will drop logs and metrics into ticket.
